intro.title: Pipes — Creation & Usage
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a custom Angular pipe that formats currency values and learn how to use both built-in and custom pipes in templates. You'll explore the core concept of pipes, which are functions that transform data for display purposes without modifying the original data. The lesson covers creating a pipe class using the @Pipe decorator, implementing the PipeTransform interface, and applying pipes in component templates using the pipe operator (|). You'll work with Angular's dependency injection system and learn how to make pipes reusable across your application. By the end, you'll understand how pipes provide a clean separation between data transformation logic and component business logic.
intro.usecase: Angular pipes are essential for data transformation in modern web applications, appearing everywhere from e-commerce product listings that format prices and dates to social media feeds that display relative timestamps like '2 hours ago'. They're commonly used in admin dashboards to format currency values, user tables to transform usernames to proper case, and financial applications to display numbers with appropriate decimal places and thousand separators. Custom pipes become particularly valuable in enterprise applications where you need consistent data formatting across components, such as transforming API response data into user-friendly display formats or creating reusable filters for search results.
